what.text: Follistatin is a protein the body makes. It binds and blocks myostatin, a signal that limits muscle growth, and activin. Because it also acts on the pituitary’s activin–inhibin system, it can lower follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH), a reproductive hormone.

src.label: Al-Zaidy SA, et al. J Neuromuscul Dis 2015 (review)

what.text: The gene makes several forms. “FS344” (follistatin 344) is one spliced form; it is processed into FS315, which circulates in the blood and binds activin about ten times less strongly than the FS288 form. Researchers chose FS344 for gene therapy partly for this reason.

src.label: Al-Zaidy SA, et al. J Neuromuscul Dis 2015 (review)
Mendell JR, et al. Mol Ther 2015

what.text: In human trials, follistatin has been given as gene therapy: a virus (AAV) or a DNA ring (plasmid) containing the FS344 gene is injected into muscle so the body makes the protein. The protein itself has not been tested as an injected drug in a published trial. FDA has found “Follistatin-344” promoted online in multi-ingredient compounded products.

what.text: Follistatin is a protein, not a short peptide. The human data are from small gene therapy trials in muscle disease.

research.text: All human data on follistatin come from small gene therapy trials. The published ones treated 6 patients with Becker muscular dystrophy and 6 people with inclusion body myositis, without placebo groups. Newer plasmid and AAV trials in healthy or older adults have no published results.
Each study is listed below as it was run.

research.title: Becker muscular dystrophy, AAV1.CMV.FS344, 2015

facts.v: open-label, two dose groups, no placebo (NCT01519349)
6 patients with Becker muscular dystrophy, an inherited muscle disease that affects males
a single set of injections of the FS344 gene, delivered by an AAV1 virus, into both thigh (quadriceps) muscles
main goal: distance walked in 6 minutes; also muscle biopsies

research.found: 4 of 6 walked farther (by 29 to 125 meters); 2 showed no change. Biopsies showed less scarring in muscle. No adverse effects were reported.

src.label: Mendell JR, et al. Mol Ther 2015
ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01519349

research.meta: USA · 2017 · Open-label, compared with untreated patients
research.title: Sporadic inclusion body myositis, AAV1 FS344, 2017

facts.v: open-label, with an exercise program; compared with 8 untreated patients matched for age, sex and baseline (not randomized)
6 people with sporadic inclusion body myositis, a muscle disease most common in men over 50
the FS344 gene by AAV1 virus into both thigh muscles
distance walked in 6 minutes, over about a year

research.found: Walking distance rose by a median 56 meters a year in treated people and fell by 25.8 meters in untreated ones. Four of six improved by 58 to 153 meters; two barely changed.

research.text: Two more trials are listed: a completed early pilot of combined follistatin and klotho plasmid gene therapy in 14 adults aged 50 to 80 (NCT07285629), and a Phase 1/2a trial of AAV9-follistatin, alone or with a VEGF plasmid, recruiting 12 adults with age-related muscle decline in Honduras (NCT07443826). Neither has published results.

research.text: In cynomolgus monkeys, the FS344 gene injected into the thigh muscle by AAV1 led to larger, stronger muscles that lasted, with no abnormal changes found in key organs. The authors had filed a patent on the approach.

after.title: Sport
after.text: Follistatin is prohibited at all times under class S4.3 (agents preventing activin receptor IIB activation) of the 2026 Prohibited List, which names it as a myostatin-binding protein: “Myostatin-binding proteins (e.g. follistatin, myostatin propeptide).” S4.3 substances are not “specified substances.” Follistatin gene therapy also falls under M3 (gene and cell doping), which bans the use of nucleic acids that may alter gene expression. The 2027 list keeps both entries.

side.text: The Becker trial reported no adverse effects. The published gene therapy trials treated only 12 people in total. Long-term safety of follistatin gene therapy is not known.

items.text: no adverse effects in the 6-patient Becker trial; the inclusion body myositis paper does not report treatment-related harms in its abstract.

items.text: follistatin can lower FSH, a pituitary hormone involved in reproduction, through the activin–inhibin system. This is one reason researchers chose the FS344 form. No published trial reporting sperm or fertility in men was found.

src.label: Al-Zaidy SA, et al. J Neuromuscul Dis 2015 (review)

items.text: the trials used viral or plasmid gene delivery, which is meant to make the body produce follistatin for a long time. The newer plasmid and AAV9 trials list side effects as their main outcome but have not posted results.
